newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon snubs Rwanda genocide tribunal official.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon snubs Rwanda genocide tribunal official.

text.p: The registrar of the International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda's 1994 massacres accused Cameroon on Wednesday of dragging its feet over the handover of four genocide suspects for trial.
Andronico Adede said he was preparing to return to the tribunal's headquarters in Arusha, Tanzania, after failing to get an audience with the Cameroon justice minister for the third straight day.
"Since June I have been to Cameroon every month," Adede told Reuters. "I have given the Cameroon government a complete dossier on the matter but I don't understand what is happening."
Adede arrived in Yaounde on Monday to arrange the transfer to Arusha of the four most wanted genocide suspects, including former army colonel Theoneste Bagosora.

Cameroon courts have ruled in favour of extraditing Bagosora and 11 other men. For now the tribunal only wants Bagosora and three other prime suspects -- Ferdinand Nahimana, Anatole Nsengiyumva, a former chief of military intelligence and Andre Ntagerura, a former transport and communications minister.
Adede said he had been kept waiting in a hotel room for a promised appointment with new Justice Minister Laurent Esso.
"Obviously there is a new government, but it seems to me the new justice minister was the director of the political department at the presidency so he is familiar with this case," Adede said.
A senior justice ministry official told Reuters he had sent a third dossier on the matter to the minister on Wednesday.

"Even officials of the United States embassy came to see me yesterday. They are very interested in this case. I told them the file was with the presidency," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

"In my report I reminded my superiors of the risks of sanctions to Cameroon," he said. "Sixty days after the request for the transfer (of suspects) Cameroon risks being sanctioned by the United Nations (if it does not comply). I hope it doesn't come to that." The tribunal demanded the transfer on June 3.

Cameroon's courts have ruled that the tribunal, which is investigating the killing by Rwandan Hutu hardliners of up to a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus, has the right to extradite Bagosora and the 11 others held in Cameroon.
They ruled that the U.N. court outranked national courts in international law. They declined to rule on a Rwandan extradition request.
Bagosora was a top official at the defence ministry during the massacres and is one of Rwanda's most wanted men.
Officials say that the handover of the suspects depends on the go-ahead from Cameroon President Paul Biya, which they describe as an administrative formality.
